title: Jana Nayagan Review: Vijay's Farewell Film Delivers Fan Service and Political Punch
excerpt: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Thalapathy Vijay's swansong blends high-octane action with political messaging, earning mixed-to-positive reviews as a fitting curtain call for the superstar's three-decade career.
body:
• Jana Nayagan, Thalapathy Vijay's final film before full-time politics, released on July 23, 2026, after months of delays and certification hurdles
  • The ₹300 crore political action thriller earned 3 to 3.5 out of 5 stars from critics, praised for Vijay's screen presence and Anirudh Ravichander's score, but criticized for a predictable screenplay
  • Bobby Deol plays the menacing antagonist opposite Vijay's former police officer character, with the film adapted from the Telugu hit Bhagavanth Kesari
  • The film features cameos by directors Atlee, Lokesh Kanagaraj, and Nelson Dilipkumar as a tribute to Vijay's cinematic legacy

Vijay Exits Cinema on His Own Terms

After over three decades and dozens of blockbusters, Thalapathy Vijay — now Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister — has delivered what he calls his final act as a film actor. Jana Nayagan (released as Jan Neta in Hindi and Jana Nayakudu in Telugu) hit theaters worldwide on July 23, 2026, and early reviews suggest it is exactly what fans expected: a larger-than-life celebration of the superstar, with all the slow-motion entries, thunderous dialogue, and political messaging that have defined his career.

https://x.com/filmfare/status/2080225583741759968

Directed by H. Vinoth and produced by Venkat K. Narayana under KVN Productions in association with Zee Studios, the film had a turbulent path to release. Originally slated for January 2026, it was delayed by CBFC certification battles, online leaks, and multiple postponements. None of it dampened the frenzy. Theaters across Tamil Nadu reported scenes resembling cricket stadiums, with whistles, cheering, and celebrations accompanying every frame of Vijay's performance.

A Familiar Story With High-Octane Execution

At its core, Jana Nayagan follows Vetri Kondan, a former police officer who becomes the foster father of a young girl named Viji after her father's death. Determined to fulfill her parents' wish of seeing her become a military officer, Vetri's life takes a dangerous turn when he uncovers a criminal network operating under the guise of a toy importer. His pursuit leads him to John Himmler, a ruthless antagonist played by Bobby Deol, whose menacing screen presence fuels the film's high-stakes confrontations.

The screenplay, adapted from Nandamuri Balakrishna's Telugu hit Bhagavanth Kesari with a story credit to Anil Ravipudi, keeps the original's action framework while layering in political themes about democracy, institutional corruption, and governance — subjects that carry unmistakable resonance given Vijay's real-life political career.

"Jana Nayagan may not rank among Vijay's strongest films, nor does it redefine the political action genre. Yet the film succeeds because it understands exactly what it wants to be."

— IndiaForums review

Strong Performances, Uneven Writing

Critics are unanimous on one point: the film belongs entirely to Vijay. His command over every frame — whether in emotional scenes with his on-screen daughter, explosive action sequences, or the showstopping "Thalapathy Kacheri" dance number that doubles as an emotional farewell — cements why he remained one of Indian cinema's biggest draws for three decades.

Mamitha Baiju emerged as a standout, earning praise for her portrayal of Viji and forging genuine emotional chemistry with Vijay. Bobby Deol brings intimidation and physical menace to the villain role, though reviewers noted his character lacks the psychological depth to become a truly compelling rival. Pooja Hegde, playing a journalist and love interest, was widely described as underutilized despite a charming performance. Veteran actors Prakash Raj, Priyamani, Gautham Vasudev Menon, and Nassar round out the ensemble.

Pinkvilla awarded the film 3 out of 5 stars, while IndiaForums and ZoomTV both gave it 3.5 out of 5, a consensus that positions the film as a solid entertainer rather than a cinematic landmark.

Anirudh's Score Elevates the Spectacle

If there is a unanimous hero beyond Vijay himself, it is composer Anirudh Ravichander. Reviewers across publications singled out his background score as the film's secret weapon — elevating every heroic moment, adding urgency to action sequences, and lending emotional weight to quieter scenes. The film also tackles social themes including women's empowerment, child safety awareness, and financial independence, though critics noted these messages occasionally veer into preachy territory.

The production's ₹300 crore budget is visible on screen, with strong cinematography by Sathyan Sooryan in outdoor and action sequences. However, CGI and VFX work drew criticism for appearing unfinished, and the film's runtime tested patience even among sympathetic reviewers.

"Every callback, every whistle-worthy entry and every emotional beat is designed to remind viewers why Vijay became one of Indian cinema's biggest icons in the first place."

— IndiaForums

A Farewell Designed for the Faithful

The film includes cameos by directors Atlee, Lokesh Kanagaraj, and Nelson Dilipkumarkumar, along with Anirudh himself — a collective tribute to the collaborators who shaped Vijay's latter-career blockbusters. It also pays homage to M.G. Ramachandran, another Tamil actor who successfully transitioned into politics, positioning Vijay firmly within that lineage.

For the Indian diaspora, Jana Nayagan arrives as a cultural event transcending cinema. Vijay's political journey — from actor to party leader to Chief Minister — mirrors the storied tradition of South Indian stars wielding enormous influence beyond the screen. The film's worldwide release, spanning Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada, and Malayalam, ensures his farewell reaches every pocket of the global audience that followed his career.

Whether Jana Nayagan endures as great cinema is debatable. Whether it succeeds as a farewell is not. For a fanbase that stood by Vijay through decades and political transformation, this is the curtain call they wanted — messy, massive, and unapologetically his.
